title: QRÖMELIFE
excerpt: Quavo has released *QRÖMELIFE*, his third solo album, with a different center of gravity from *Rocket Power*.
body:
Quavo has released *QRÖMELIFE*, his third solo album, with a different center of gravity from *Rocket Power*. That record arrived close to Takeoff's death and was built around grief. The loss is still present here, but it no longer has to carry the entire album. Family, ambition, pleasure and the work of simply continuing all get space of their own, allowing the record to look beyond mourning without pretending that the absence has become less important.

Pharrell Williams was the main creative partner behind the record, but the collaboration was less about replacing Quavo's sound than recovering parts of it. The rapper kept returning in interviews to range and to the melodic instincts that made him distinctive inside and outside Migos. He wanted one project to hold more of those versions of himself at once. *QRÖMELIFE* stays rooted in the Atlanta sound around him while giving his solo delivery more room to shift between moods.

The title comes from his own idea of being "qrome," a word he links to "chromosome." He uses it for the condition of carrying something difficult and still getting up to handle ordinary life. His example is deliberately unglamorous. Something can happen to you, and the next morning you still have to go to work. That keeps the concept away from a tidy recovery story. On *QRÖMELIFE*, perseverance is not presented as forgetting what happened. It is learning to live with the experience already built into you.

[apple:album:6817200688]

"Away" brings Offset back onto one of his solo albums after the split that left the future of Migos uncertain even before Takeoff's death. The two repaired their relationship in the years that followed, and the reunion matters because neither has treated it as a substitute for the missing third member. They are working on more Migos music, but any release under that name would have to honor Takeoff and benefit his estate. Their reunion can lead to new Migos music, but it does not restore the trio.

Fatherhood gives the album its most concrete change in perspective. He recently revealed that he has become a father to a daughter, and he has connected the responsibility directly to losing his own father when he was four. He wants to be present for the parts of his child's life that he never had a father there to see. The short film released with *QRÖMELIFE* moves through Takeoff, the years that followed and the work on the new album before ending with him holding his daughter. The film stops there, with a father who lost his own at four holding the child he now plans to raise differently.
